claims.text: The compositional complexity of HEAs slows overall cation diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion in HEAs causes preferential surface enrichment of high-valence oxide-forming elements such as Cr or Al.
Surface enrichment of Cr or Al promotes formation of protective Cr2O3 or Al2O3.
Al2O3 is a slow-growing and high-temperature-resistant protective oxide.
Increasing Al content can replace a manganese-rich oxide layer with a protective Al2O3 layer.
Increasing Al content can change oxidation kinetics from parabolic to logarithmic.
Increasing Al content can reduce oxide-scale thickness substantially.
The same beneficial concentration trend applies generally to either Al or Cr in HEAs.
HEAs form thinner, slower-growing oxide scales than binary or ternary alloys having matched Cr or Al content.
HEA oxide scales are more adherent than those on matched binary or ternary alloys.
Faster bulk diffusion in simpler alloys produces thicker, less uniform, or less adherent oxide scales.
Oxide-scale thickness, morphology, adhesion, phase composition, and interfacial elemental segregation mediate the oxidation response.
A controlled comparison should match the oxide-forming-element content of HEAs and conventional binary or ternary alloys while applying the same oxidation conditions.
The proposed mechanism is applicable at temperatures of at least 800 degrees Celsius under controlled oxygen partial pressure.
The proposed mechanism requires a homogenized microstructure with minimized initial segregation.
Oxidation kinetics can be measured by thermogravimetric weight gain, while microscopy and spectroscopy can assess scale thickness, morphology, phases, adhesion, and segregation.
Failure to observe a statistically significant protective advantage or a trend with increasing oxide-forming-element content would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome expect slower oxide growth in HEAs, but the falsification rule lists 'faster growth kinetics' alongside reduction in thickness and improved adhesion as though it were an expected protective advantage. This likely should read 'slower growth kinetics.'
